headline: Right-of-way proceedings for 1720 Spear Street start, with February 10th site visit and hearing set.
summary: A city review board denied a final plat application for 1720 Spear Street on July 10, 2026, in part because the applicant did not provide right-of-way for the official city map. The 120-day deadline to start proceedings would have ended November 7th, 2026. Staff is talking with the property owners and hopes the hearing can be canceled if other agreements are reached. Staff also asked members to send their top five legislative priorities by the end of the day Tuesday.
decisions: Approved unanimously to start right-of-way proceedings for 1720 Spear Street and open the public hearing.
Approved unanimously setting February 10th for the site visit at 3:00 p.m. and the hearing at 5:00.
Continued the public hearing to the selected dates and directed staff to follow notice and statutory requirements.
discussion: Hearing dates: Staff said the February 10th dates leave time for notice requirements and for talks with the property owners. Staff also said the site visit could be done from a paved road beside the property.

Legislative priorities: Members discussed how many priorities to send the legislative delegation, with suggestions from three to ten, and most favoring five or fewer. Staff recommended four: local options tax, transportation, municipal authority on energy codes, and e-moto sales.

Local options tax: Members discussed a 2% local option tax charter change modeled on Stowe's, and whether the city's share, now 0.8, should rise. Staff said state law limits access to data on which businesses produce the tax receipts.

I move that we select February 10th at 3:00 p.m. as the date and time for the, uh, site visit to examine the premises, and the public hear and conduct the public hearing on necessity and compensation or damages. ...Aye. Aye. It's also unanimous.
